_usage: Copy this file to config.json or ~/.config/mqttaudio/config.json and customize for your setup
_editor: Prefer a guided setup? Run 'mqttaudio --configure' to build or edit a config interactively, with explanations, pickers, and live device testing

_notes: server: MQTT broker hostname or IP address
port: MQTT broker port (default: 1883)
topic: MQTT topic to subscribe to (required). Supports wildcards like 'audio/#'
client_id: MQTT client ID. If null, auto-generates a random 'mqttaudio_<hex>' id
reconnect_delay_seconds: Wait time before reconnecting after disconnect
device: Exact Device ID from --list-devices. null = system default. On Linux copy the ALSA ID (e.g. plughw:CARD=HD,DEV=0), not the Description
sample_rate: Output sample rate in Hz. Common values: 44100, 48000, 96000
buffer_size: Audio buffer size in frames. Smaller = lower latency but higher CPU
Common values: 256 (low latency), 512 (balanced), 1024 (high compatibility)
channel_aliases: Optional mapping of friendly channel names to channel indices
channel_volumes: Per-channel calibration (0.0-1.0) to compensate for hardware differences
enabled: Enable the disk cache for downloaded files. false = downloads
play from memory only and are re-fetched after a restart
directory: Directory for cache storage. ~ expands to user home
revalidate_after_seconds: How long a cached URL is served before asking the
server whether it changed (conditional request via ETag/Last-Modified).
0 = check on every access; higher = fewer checks. A changed file is
re-downloaded automatically; an unreachable server falls back to the cache
allowed_directories: Whitelist of directories for local file access
When non-empty, play/precache paths must resolve inside one of these
directories (symlinks followed, ../ traversal blocked)
Empty array = local file access is unrestricted
Paths can use ~ for user home directory
level: Log level - 'error', 'warn', 'info', 'debug', or 'trace'
verbose: Legacy verbose mode. Equivalent to level: 'debug'
device: Input device name. null = system default. Use --list-inputs to see options
Example: 'plughw:CARD=UMC1820,DEV=0'
On Linux prefer the 'plughw:' alias of a card: capture is read as 32-bit float
and plughw: converts from the card's native format
volume: Input volume gain (0.0-4.0, 1.0 = unity)
voice_id: Voice name, used by input_volume/input_mute commands and ducking rules
activity_threshold: Peak level (0.0-1.0) above which this input counts as speaking,
letting its voice_id trigger ducking rules as primary_voice. null = detection off
activity_hold_ms: How long activity persists after the level drops (rides out pauses)
latency_ms: Buffer latency (5-500). 20-30 is a good starting point for live mics
channels: Capture channels to open. null = smallest count covering every source_channel
sample_rate: Capture rate to request. null = match the output rate and skip resampling
routes: source_channel (mic input, 0-indexed) to dest_channel (speaker output)
Two source channels sharing a dest_channel are summed there
dest_channel may use a name from audio.channel_aliases
